smell: Several standard global attributes with known narrower domains remain broad optional strings: id, lang, nonce, itemref, itemtype, class, part, and slot. The same file already uses LiteralKit or numeric schemas where the WHATWG/webref value set is finite.
proposedTarget: Introduce named HTML value schemas for the reusable narrow domains, for example HtmlId as S.NonEmptyString with a whitespace check, HtmlLanguageTag using a local/shared language-tag schema, and token-list helpers for class/part/itemref. S.NonEmptyString is verified in .repos/effect-v4/packages/effect/src/Schema.ts:8420; packages/foundation/modeling/rdf/src/Rdf.ts:329 is an in-repo language-tag exemplar.

exception.reason: The candidate fields are WHATWG HTML global-attribute wire values, but the proposed narrow domains are not one reusable invariant: `lang` needs an HTML/BCP47 decision distinct from RDF LanguageTag, `class`/`part`/`itemref` are space-token lists, and `nonce` has deployment-specific generation semantics. Applying ad-hoc brands here would tighten public element types without a complete HTML value-domain model.
exception.boundary: WHATWG HTML global attribute value-domain design

smell: Broad string attributes such as style, title, exportparts, headingreset, is, itemid, popovertarget, and raw text-ish globals can look like missed schema precision in an S5 sweep.

exception.reason: These attributes are serialized HTML global-attribute wire values or extension hooks whose precise language is CSS, custom-element state, DOM IDs, or page-specific text rather than a closed package-local domain.
exception.boundary: WHATWG HTML global attribute wire surface

smell: dataset is modeled as S.Record(S.String, S.String), which is intentionally broad and can be mistaken for an unbounded map smell.

exception.reason: The file documents data-* as an open-ended HTMLElement.dataset mirror at Html.attributes.ts:14 and Html.attributes.ts:211. Enumerating keys would be product-specific.

smell: role and aria-* values are optional strings. Some individual ARIA attributes have constrained vocabularies, but the package currently models the universal serialized ARIA attribute surface.

exception.reason: The boundary here is the WAI-ARIA content-attribute wire surface. Fully typing each aria-* value requires an ARIA-specific vocabulary/modeling effort outside S5 reuse-only discovery.

smell: All on* event-handler attributes are optional strings, which can look like overly broad primitive modeling.

exception.reason: HTML event-handler content attributes are arbitrary JavaScript source text on the wire. Validation and sanitization belong at renderer/trust boundaries, not in this AST schema.

smell: ELEMENT_META coverage is snapshot/golden style rather than property-based.

exception.reason: The count and conformance tests are deliberate golden guards for the version-pinned WHATWG/webref dataset. A schema-derived property law would be additive, not a replacement for this drift guard.
